chunks: He said: al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi al-Warraq informed me, he said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi al-Katib narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Mahboob narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said:
A believer remains in prayer as long as he is in the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whether standing, sitting, or lying down.

Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth: Our Lord, You have not created this in vain. Glory be to You! So protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'

key_terms.ذكر الله: Dhikr (remembrance of God) - continuous awareness and devotion to Allah in all states and postures
key_terms.صلاة: Salat (prayer) - here used broadly to encompass any form of worship and remembrance, not limited to the formal ritual prayer

ai.seo_question: Is a believer in prayer as long as they remember Allah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that the state of prayer extends beyond formal ritual to encompass all forms of dhikr (remembrance of God). He affirmed to his companion Abu Hamza al-Thumali that whether one is standing, sitting, or lying down, constant remembrance of God is itself a form of prayer. He supports this with Quran 3:191, which praises those who remember God in every posture and reflect upon creation.
